summary: Cold protocol-wide economic scan of the NFT mint/debt dispatcher->hook suite. Four targeted hunts (phUSD >100% over-mint, DelayRelease hold-and-release window, NFTMinterV2 price growth, Uniboost donation+LP MEV) all resolve to owner-knowing configuration or existing-ledger echoes. NO new High/Medium economic vector: no unprivileged actor can extract value, mint unbacked phUSD, or profit from a round-trip. Findings recorded as informational confirmations to preserve recall (Law 1), each tied to its suppression boundary.

findings.description: NudgeRatchetMintDebtHook permits ratio up to MAX_RATIO=200, so pull() can mint up to 2x the dispatched USDC (scaled 1e12) as phUSD, versus the 50% cap on UniboostMintDebtHook/BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook. Even in the ideal case where NudgeRatchet sweeps 100% of USDC to the batchMinter, the accrued phUSD can be double the USDC that reached the sink.
findings.economicImpact: At ratio>100 the phUSD minted structurally exceeds the USDC forwarded (the 'nudge reward' over-issuance). Whether this is under-backed depends entirely on phUSD's external collateral model, which is out of scope (DEDUP-001).
findings.whyNotNew: The ratio is set only by onlyOwner setRatio; default is 100 and MAX_RATIO=200 is documented in NatSpec as the intended inclusive nudge-reward bound. Setting 2x is a knowing, obvious owner action (Law 3 trusted, not a footgun -- the consequence is exactly what the parameter name/NatSpec advertise). The unbacked-mint concern itself is the suppressed DEDUP-001 external-backing boundary. No distinct new over-mint vector arises: the >100% ceiling does not add any unprivileged-actor path beyond DEDUP-001's framing, it only widens an owner-configured knob. Confirmed intended; do not escalate.

findings.description: Debt accrues (and phUSD can be pulled/minted) at dispatch while the backing USDC is HELD on the dispatcher, released later by a whitelisted releaser. rescueERC20 can withdraw the held _token (USDC). This creates an intended admin-controlled window in which realised phUSD is not yet backed at the batchMinter sink, and a residual owner path to permanently under-back already-pulled debt.
findings.economicImpact: System-level phUSD is transiently under-collateralised at the sink during the hold window (USDC still on the dispatcher, conserved). rescueERC20 on _token after a pull leaves debt permanently under-backed.
findings.whyNotNew: Backing is conserved (release only relocates existing USDC); the only ways to move it are onlyReleaser release() and onlyOwner rescueERC20 -- both trusted. No unprivileged actor can create unbacked phUSD. The decoupling is documented accepted design (F-01-043 open informational), the pause-doesn't-freeze-custody angle is L-12, and the dropped bal>=amount tripwire is Q-11. Checked for a distinct new econ angle (e.g. hold-window x ratio>100 compounding): it reduces to the same DEDUP-001 external-backing question, no unprivileged path. No new finding.
findings.affectedParties: phUSD holders (during hold window, if peg assumes sink funding)

findings.description: Ascending primary-sale price: each mint pays the OLD price (transferFrom at `price`, event emits `price`), then price grows monotonically. CEI-correct (price grown before dispatch). Growth floors, rounding the NEXT price marginally in the buyer's favour by dust.
findings.economicImpact: None exploitable. Monotonic ascending price with no sell-back / redemption leg -- there is no round-trip to extract from. First mover pays least (expected primary-issuance economics), no last-mover advantage, no sandwich profit (no sell side). Minting to raise a rival's price costs the griefer a full paid mint, so no cheap griefing.
findings.whyNotNew: Basis-point growth compounding is known-issue #6 (OOS). The floor-rounding on price growth is negligible dust and cannot be round-tripped (NFTs are not redeemable to USDC in these contracts). The onERC1155Received re-entry on mint just pays the new higher price (no economic gain -- ledger L-01, qa-bundled). mintFor bypasses payment/price but is authorizedMinter-gated (trusted). No new finding.

findings.description: Uniboost carves donationSplit% of gross prime to recipient via plain safeTransfer (no swap, MEV-free), retains the rest, and accrues debt on the GROSS amount. Separate keeper-gated pool() swaps retained prime->pair->~half target and addLiquidity with 0/0 min amounts, bounded by keeper-supplied minPairOut/minTargetOut/minLP floors.
findings.economicImpact: pool() swaps are sandwich-exposed but bounded by keeper floors (minLP post-check reverts a manipulated add). Debt-on-gross with the 50%-capped hook means phUSD <= 0.5x gross regardless of donation split, so the position stays over-backed. Donation split rounds down (favours retained protocol LP).
findings.whyNotNew: The keeper-gated addLiquidity-0/0 sandwich exposure is exactly ledger L-06 (Balancer lineage, stays Low); the missing hookTypeId guard (wrong hook -> zero debt, fail-open UNDER-accrual = over-backed, safe direction) is L-09; the same-pool-in-batch floor staleness via MultiPooler is L-11. No new value-leak beyond these: donation transfer is swap-free, rounding favours the protocol, and no unprivileged actor reaches pool() (onlyAuthorizedPooler trusted keeper). No new finding.
